The spectral data point to an unsaturated carboxylic acid. The very broad IR absorption at 3000 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of the O–H stretch of a carboxylic acid. The strong peaks at 1700 cm⁻¹ (C=O) and 1650 cm⁻¹ (C=C) indicate the presence of both a carbonyl and an alkene. Vinyl hydrogens in the ¹H NMR confirm the alkene, and the mass spectral fragment at m/z = 45 is typical of the COOH⁺ ion. 

A carboxylic acid requires two oxygen atoms, ruling out C₆H₁₂O and C₆H₁₀O. C₆H₁₂O₂ has only one degree of unsaturation, which is insufficient for both a C=O and a C=C bond. C₆H₁₀O₂ has two degrees of unsaturation, perfectly accommodating one carbonyl and one alkene.

Answer: B
